scenario.summary: CL-UNK-1211 is an AI-assisted campaign targeting government Linux infrastructure to exfiltrate mailboxes and sensitive databases. The attackers utilize custom Go-based backdoors (SysGoRAT), extensive web shell deployments, and creative credential theft such as hijacking the sudo command through .bashrc modifications.

meta.rationale: Focus the hunt on Linux-based mail servers (qmail, postfix) and database servers, as these are the primary targets for the collection techniques described in the CL-UNK-1211 report.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using in-memory reverse shells to conduct interactive discovery and exfiltrate government mailboxes, likely use AI-assisted scripting patterns for efficiency.

blind_spots.risk: If the bash redirect is executed via an eval or inside a pre-existing shell without a new process launch, the command line might not be visible in hb_process_activity.
blind_spots.question: whether the redirect pattern bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ was executed inside a complex script
blind_spots.requires: command-line auditing or script block logging on Linux

blind_spots.risk: WebSocket traffic (wss://) is encrypted; hb_network_connection sees only the IP and port, preventing confirmation of the WebSocket protocol or URI path without a decrypting proxy.
blind_spots.question: whether the WebSocket traffic was for SysGoRAT or a benign service

hunt.name: Interactive Shells and Data Collection (CL-UNK-1211)
hunt.description: This hunt focuses on the active intrusion phase of the CL-UNK-1211 campaign. It identifies behavioral indicators of interactive reverse shells (Netcat, Bash redirects, and Python subprocesses) which the attacker uses to enumerate and compress mailbox data for exfiltration. The hunt uses a gated flow, first identifying the characteristic shell patterns before fanning out to check for known C2 traffic and unusual mailbox access across the Linux estate.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, process_cmd_line, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ((LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%mkfifo%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%nc %') OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/dev/tcp/%') OR (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%socket.socket%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%subprocess.call%')) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the characteristic behavioral patterns of in-memory reverse shells using pipes, redirects, or scripted sockets.
config.expected_signal: Rows containing shell commands that redirect I/O to network sockets. Silence indicates no shell redirection was captured in the process logs during the window.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/var/qmail/%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/maildir/%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/cur/%') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%zip %' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%tar %' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%find %') AND LOWER(process_name) NOT LIKE '%backup%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Stack-count directory enumeration and compression commands involving mail storage to identify data collection while filtering common administrative noise.
config.expected_signal: A rare command string zipping a mail directory on one or two hosts. Genuine backup processes should be frequent across the fleet.
